content: Great debts do not make for gratitude, but for revenge; and if a little benefit is not forgotten, it becomes a gnawing worm.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche
story:
Living in austere solitude across Alpine villages like Sils Maria and battling near-blindness and debilitating migraines, Nietzsche renounced conventional academia to diagnose the spiritual crisis of modern Europe. In heroic defiance of nihilism, he championed the affirmation of all existence—including pain—through the doctrine of Amor Fati (love of fate).

In formulating this reflection, Friedrich Nietzsche stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of debt. For Friedrich Nietzsche, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: How does adopting this philosophical view alter the way you handle current friction?
